programme: MEIS1, MEIS3, MSX1, HMX1, HOXC6 and HOXC8 (TALE/NKX/HOX-class homeodomain factors of the kind that pattern neural-crest and autonomic lineages) together with NPAS1 (bHLH-PAS) and ETV1 (ETS) form a neural-crest/sympathoadrenal differentiation module. HMX1, NPAS1 and ETV1 converge directly on TH, the catecholamine-synthesis enzyme, and NPAS1 additionally targets the HIF partners ARNT/ARNT2 and the hypoxia gene EPO, tying the module to hypoxia-responsive transcription.
role_in_a: In pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma this is close to the tumour's own lineage programme: these are chromaffin/paraganglion neural-crest patterning factors converging on TH, the enzyme that defines the tumour's catecholamine-secreting phenotype, and NPAS1's ARNT/ARNT2 targets sit on the same HIF axis implicated in SDHx-driven pseudohypoxic paraganglioma. ETV1 itself is reported epigenomically altered in malignant pheochromocytoma (PMID 20534969).
role_in_b: In stroke, none of these eight factors has a documented role in the retrieved record. The plausible physiological bridge runs downstream of the programme rather than through it: catecholamine release (the TH product this module converges on) and hypoxia-response signalling (the ARNT/EPO axis NPAS1 touches) are both recognised participants in stroke pathophysiology, but that is a hormonal/physiological link, not a transcriptional one documented for these factors in cerebrovascular or neuronal tissue.
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would be catecholamine biology: a tumour that autonomously oversecretes catecholamines via this same TH-converging programme is a recognised cause of hypertensive-crisis stroke in clinical practice — but nothing in this record shows the transcriptional module itself, as opposed to its hormonal output, operating in stroke tissue.
reasoning: The programme is nameable purely from the factors' known developmental biology (homeodomain/bHLH-PAS/ETS patterning factors converging on TH), which keeps this from being incoherent. But only one carrying factor (ETV1) is placed in either disease by a retrieved paper, none is placed in stroke, and the reader's own summary states no factor links to both diseases or their mechanism — so any connection rests on general catecholamine physiology rather than on anything retrieved for this pair.
support: PMID 20534969 — places ETV1, a carrying factor, in pheochromocytoma via epigenomic analysis of malignant tumours, consistent with reactivation of this differentiation programme. PMID 41989510 — places MECP2, not a carrying factor here, in an ischemia-reperfusion stroke model as a microRNA target; it does not bear on the catecholaminergic/homeodomain module.
how_to_falsify: ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for MEIS1, HMX1, NPAS1 and ETV1 in peri-infarct or cerebrovascular tissue from a stroke model: if none occupies TH or ARNT/ARNT2 regulatory regions outside chromaffin-lineage cells, the module is pheochromocytoma-specific and its stroke recurrence is coincidental; demonstrated occupancy and catecholamine-pathway activation in ischemic brain/vascular tissue would instead support a genuine shared transcriptional axis rather than a purely hormonal one.
caveats: Support ranges only 14-18 of 30 patient-group comparisons for every factor here (no near-unanimous factor), across just 4 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance itself is modest. HOXB4 — the classic MEIS1 hematopoietic-complex partner — appears only in the single-view exclusion list, so this account should not lean on the MEIS1-HOXB4 hematopoietic stem-cell axis; the HOX partners that did survive (HOXC6, HOXC8) are a different pairing. The tissue-generic exclusion list is dominated by immune/myeloid factors (SPI1, IRF8, FOS, JUNB), arguing against an immune-cell explanation and consistent with a developmental/neuroendocrine reading, but 'blood' as the stroke tissue label likely reflects the expression-data source rather than the anatomical site of stroke pathology, which limits how literally the adrenal|blood pairing should be read anatomically.
